subject: anaesthesia
title: Intravenous Induction: Propofol, Pain on Injection, and Infusion Syndrome

steps.title: Propofol Chemical Formulation
steps.tx: **Propofol lipid emulsion formulation** consists of 2,6-diisopropylphenol dissolved in a white aqueous emulsion containing 10 percent soybean oil, 2.25 percent glycerol, and 1.2 percent purified egg phosphatide. Propofol acts by selectively enhancing inhibitory gamma-aminobutyric acid type A (GABA-A) receptor neurotransmission, producing smooth loss of consciousness within 30 to 45 seconds following a standard induction bolus of 1.5 to 2.5 milligrams per kilogram.

steps.title: Pain on Injection Mechanisms
steps.tx: **Vascular pain on propofol injection** occurs in up to 70 percent of patients receiving an injection through small dorsal hand veins, caused by direct irritation of venous adventitia and release of local kininogens. Pain is dramatically mitigated by selecting large antecubital veins, co-administering 20 to 40 milligrams of intravenous lignocaine (either mixed with propofol or preceded by a venous occlusion tourniquet for 30 seconds), or pre-treating with intravenous ketamine.

steps.title: Propofol Antiemetic Actions
steps.tx: **Antiemetic properties of propofol** distinguish it from all other intravenous induction agents: sub-hypnotic doses (10 to 20 milligram boluses or maintenance infusions at 10 to 30 micrograms per kilogram per minute) exert potent antiemetic activity by direct antagonism of dopamine D2 and serotonin 5-HT3 receptors within the chemoreceptor trigger zone and area postrema, dramatically slashing the incidence of postoperative nausea and vomiting.

left.title: Sub-Hypnotic Propofol Therapy
points: Doses of 10 to 20 mg IV produce zero cognitive sedation
Directly depresses chemoreceptor trigger zone neurotransmission
First-line rescue agent for refractory postoperative nausea in PACU

right.title: Total Intravenous Anaesthesia (TIVA)
points: Maintenance with propofol eliminates volatile emetogens entirely
Reduces baseline PONV risk by up to 80 percent
Ideal for high-risk patients with prior history of motion sickness

steps.title: Propofol Infusion Syndrome (PRIS)
steps.tx: **Propofol infusion syndrome pathogenesis** is a lethal metabolic complication resulting from prolonged high-dose propofol infusions (exceeding 4 to 5 milligrams per kilogram per hour for greater than 48 hours), frequently in pediatric or critically ill intensive care patients. Propofol impairs mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation and free fatty acid cellular transport, precipitating severe metabolic lactic acidosis, rhabdomyolysis, hyperkalaemia, acute renal failure, and refractory bradyasystolic heart failure.

steps.title: Bacterial Contamination Hazard
steps.tx: **Bacterial sepsis risk with propofol** stems from its lipid emulsion vehicle, which lacks antimicrobial preservatives and forms an ideal growth medium for bacteria and fungal pathogens, specifically Staphylococcus aureus, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and Candida albicans. Aseptic technique mandates that opened ampoules and drawn syringes be administered within 6 to 12 hours, while continuous infusion lines must be completely discarded every 12 hours.

steps.title: Cardiovascular Hemodynamic Profile
steps.tx: **Cardiovascular depression from propofol** produces the most pronounced reduction in systemic arterial blood pressure among all intravenous induction agents, dropping mean arterial pressure by 20 to 30 percent. This hypotension results from both arterial vasodilation (reduced systemic vascular resistance) and venodilation, accompanied by blunting of the compensatory baroreceptor reflex tachycardia, requiring cautious lower dosing in elderly and hypovolemic patients.

left.title: Vascular and Myocardial Depression
points: Arteriolar smooth muscle relaxation drops afterload
Venodilation pools blood in capacitance beds dropping preload

right.title: Baroreceptor Reflex Blunting
points: Heart rate remains unchanged or drops slightly despite hypotension

steps.title: Upper Airway Reflex Blunting
steps.tx: **Profound laryngeal reflex suppression** by propofol makes it the undisputed induction agent of choice for inserting supraglottic airway devices, such as the laryngeal mask airway (LMA), without requiring neuromuscular blocking drugs. Unlike thiopentone, which leaves upper airway reflexes irritable, propofol suppresses pharyngeal and laryngeal adductor muscle tone, ensuring smooth LMA placement without coughing or gagging.

steps.title: Neurosurgical Profile of Propofol
steps.tx: **Neurosurgical actions of propofol** include paired reductions in cerebral blood flow (CBF), cerebral metabolic rate of oxygen consumption (CMRO2), and intracranial pressure (ICP), while preserving cerebral autoregulation and carbon dioxide vascular reactivity. Propofol possesses potent anticonvulsant properties, serving as a reliable second-line infusion for refractory status epilepticus in intensive care units.
